_comment: ENDORSEMENT INPUT for the signed engine-pin document (engines.json). This file is the human decision — which upstream engine build we are willing to run — and it is deliberately NOT what the client trusts: `scripts/build_engines_manifest.py` downloads every artifact listed here, reproduces its SHA-256 itself, and fails if a declared `expected_*` hash does not match. Only then does it emit engines.json for V to sign OFFLINE with the engine-pin sub-key. Every change here must land in ENGINE-TRUST-LOG.md with the same evidence. Seeded 2026-08-14 with the EXACT pins currently compiled into the client (release-assets/miners.json), so a first run reproduces today's state byte-for-byte and proves the pipeline before it is ever used to change an engine. macOS xmrig and the kawpowminer placeholders are intentionally absent: they have no fetch URL, so the client keeps using its built-in pin for them.
_stale_warning: ⛔ These entries still pin SRBMiner-MULTI 3.4.1, the build that could not mine post-fork Pearl. Every v0.6.8 client compiles in 3.5.4 and REFUSES a document that moves an engine backwards without a `downgrade` marker, so publishing this file unchanged would be rejected fleet-wide (correctly). Bump the two gpu-prl entries to the 3.5.4 hashes endorsed in ENGINE-TRUST-LOG.md epoch 2 before the first real publish.
_optional_fields: Beyond the bytes, an entry may also say HOW to call the engine and which way its version moves. All are optional; omitted means the client uses what it was compiled with. `algorithm`: the algorithm token to pass instead of the compiled-in one (short ASCII, never flag-shaped) -- accepted ONLY on kind gpu-prl, the one kind whose argv carries an algorithm token; on any other kind it is refused rather than accepted-and-ignored. `extra_args`: a LIST of argv tokens spliced in BEFORE every flag the client owns. CHANGED 2026-08-15: this is now an ALLOW-list, not a deny-list -- every flag must appear in engine_pins::extra_arg_allowlist for that engine kind, values are accepted only in the slot their flag opened and only from [A-Za-z0-9.,+_-]. Reviewed today: cpu-xmr (xmrig) has 13 RandomX/CPU tuning flags; gpu-prl, gpu-rvn and gpu-alpha have NONE, because nobody has read those engines' flag surfaces against the binaries. The deny-list-only rule failed against the engine we ship: xmrig spells --user/--pass also as --userpass, --proxy as -x and --log-file as -l, and all three were live-verified to redirect credit, transport and writes. Adding a flag is a client release, on purpose. `parser`: which compiled-in log parser reads this engine's output -- one of xmrig|kawpow|srbminer|alpha|generic; an id the client does not have refuses the whole document. `downgrade` + `downgrade_reason`: REQUIRED together when the version is not provably newer than one already in force (a real rollback, or a version string the client cannot order); the reason is shown verbatim to every miner. See docs/engine-pin-publishing.md §2a and §2b.
notes: Baseline: the engines compiled into client v0.6.7.
